name: Belgium: Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent and Bruges

destination.name: Belgium: Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent and Bruges
destination.pitch: Four cities under 80 minutes apart by train, so you sleep in two or three and ride to the rest: Flemish Primitives, Rubens, Art Nouveau and lambic for a week, planned round the museums' closing days.

because.exploration: The Marolles flea market before 10:00, Cogels-Osylei's townhouses, Ghent's legal graffiti alley, and the Kruisvest windmills path in Bruges.
because.food: Frites from Maison Antoine, moules at Chez Leon, waterzooi in the Patershol, Wittamer pralines on the Sablon, and lambic at Cantillon with 3 tastings for 9 euros.
because.culture: Van Eyck's Mystic Lamb in St Bavo's, Memling in the Groeninge, four Rubens altarpieces in Antwerp cathedral, Magritte in Brussels and Horta's own house in Saint-Gilles.
because.city: Brussels' Grand Place and Marolles, Antwerp's Het Zuid and fashion quarter, Ghent's Graslei at dusk; all four joined by trains every few minutes.

destination.caveat: Grey and wet much of the year, shoulder season included. Wednesday closes Antwerp and Bruges museums, Monday Brussels and Ghent. Tickets run 12 to 17 euros each, and Bruges is a queue on Markt from 10:30. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Brussels
cities.base: Ilot Sacre or the Sablon, inside the pentagon: walk to the Grand Place, the Sablon and dinner. You pay more and share it with the crowds.

cities.name: Antwerp
cities.base: Het Zuid, the 19th-century grid south of the centre: restaurants and bars round the old docks, Kloosterstraat antiques, a walk to the cathedral.

cities.name: Ghent
cities.base: Patershol, the old tanners' quarter turned restaurant district, 10 minutes on foot from the Gravensteen and the Graslei.

cities.name: Bruges
cities.base: Inside the canal ring by Markt and Burg, everything within 15 minutes on foot; the dearest and most crowded of the four, which is why you want to be there at 08:00.

places.name: Grand Place
places.note: The 68 by 110m square of guildhalls rebuilt after the 1695 French bombardment, UNESCO since 1998. Be there before 10:00, when the tour groups arrive; in odd years the mid-August Flower Carpet covers it for 4 days and pulls up to 200,000 people.

places.name: Manneken Pis
places.note: A 55.5cm bronze, and the one on the corner is a 1965 replica; the 1619 original is in the city museum. Smaller than you think, so look for the crowd, and check the published schedule if you want him in one of his roughly 1,000 costumes.

places.name: Atomium
places.note: The 102m steel iron crystal from the 1958 World's Fair, 6 of its 9 spheres open by escalator and lift; 17 euros. From 1 October 2026 it opens at noon, not 10:00, so check the calendar for a fall visit.

places.name: Magritte Museum
places.note: The largest Magritte collection anywhere, inside the Royal Museums of Fine Arts on rue de la Regence. Closed Mondays; weekends run 11:00 to 18:00, the desk stops selling 30 minutes before close, and in summer you book online.

places.name: Belgian Comic Strip Center
places.note: Tintin and the Smurfs inside a 1906 Horta department store; 14 euros, last tickets 17:00. Closed Mondays except in July and August, and the right answer to a wet afternoon.

places.name: Cantillon Brewery
places.note: A family lambic brewery since 1900, still fermenting on wild yeast; 9 euros self-guided with 3 tastings. Closed Wednesdays and Sundays and shut 27 July to 1 August 2026, so fix the day around it.

places.name: Delirium Cafe
places.note: A cellar bar in an alley off rue des Bouchers holding the world record for beers on sale, 2,000 and up. Touristy, but the list is real; bring cash for the busy hours, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Marolles Flea Market
places.neighborhood: Marolles, Place du Jeu de Balle
places.note: A daily flea market on the city's most working-class square since 1919; 09:00 to 14:00 weekdays, to 15:00 weekends. Get there before 10:00, before the resellers pick it over, with cash and a haggling face.

places.name: Sablon Antiques Market
places.note: Weekends only: Saturday 09:00 to 17:00, Sunday to 15:00. Dearer, polished stock compared with the Marolles, and the chocolatiers ring the same square.

places.name: Cathedral of St Michael and St Gudula
places.note: Free Gothic cathedral above Central Station; Saturday closes at 17:00 and Sunday opens only at 13:00, with no visits during services. The 11th-century crypt under the choir is 4 euros by appointment.

places.name: Horta Museum
places.note: Victor Horta's own Art Nouveau house and studio, 1898 to 1901. Weekdays it opens only at 14:00 (weekends 11:00), closed Mondays; 14 euros, free the first Sunday of the month.

places.name: Sablon chocolatiers (Wittamer, Marcolini)
places.note: Wittamer has been on the square since 1910; pralines are 3 to 5 euros each, boxes from about 15, and its cafe does a proper pastry. Skip the chain shops near the Grand Place, which mark up for the walk-by trade.

places.name: Maison Antoine
places.note: Frites since 1948, double fried in beef fat; order andalouse or samurai sauce. No seats, so carry the cone to a cafe terrace on the square and buy a drink there, and expect a queue at lunch and after 20:00.

places.name: Chez Leon
places.note: Moules-frites since 1893 on the street where every other terrace hard-sells you; this is the one with the name. Order the mariniere or white wine pot, 25 to 30 euros, and ignore the neighbours.

places.name: Moules-frites at Place Sainte-Catherine
places.note: The old fish market square, where locals eat seafood instead of on rue des Bouchers; moules-frites and oyster bars round the square. Come early evening for a terrace seat in summer.

places.name: Autoworld
places.note: 250 cars from 1899 on, in the Cinquantenaire exhibition hall; open daily, to 18:00 at weekends. The combined ticket with Art and History and the Army Museum pays if you do two.

places.name: Cinquantenaire Park
places.note: The 1880 jubilee park and its triumphal arch, free and open any time. Walk it early or at golden hour and carry on to Place Jourdan for frites.

places.name: Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert
places.note: An 1847 glass-vaulted arcade, one of Europe's oldest, with the Neuhaus flagship, a cinema and cafes. Free and dry: the route between the Grand Place and rue des Bouchers on a wet day.

places.name: Cathedral of Our Lady
places.note: Belgium's largest Gothic church, spire done in 1521, with four Rubens altarpieces including the Elevation and the Descent from the Cross; 12 euros. Saturday it closes at 15:00 and Sunday opens at 13:00.

places.name: Rubens House
places.note: The residence itself is shut for renovation in 2026; what is open is the Rubens Experience, the library and the garden with his portico, 12 euros (garden only 8). Closed Wednesdays.

places.name: MAS (Museum aan de Stroom)
places.note: A 10-storey red stone spiral on the old docks about port and trade, 12 euros; the rooftop 360 over the Scheldt is free without a ticket. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Museum Plantin-Moretus
places.note: The printing dynasty's house, workshop and shop, UNESCO listed, with the two oldest surviving presses in the world. Under-visited; closed Mondays, and hours vary, check.

places.name: DIVA
places.note: Jewellery, silver and diamonds at Suikerrui 17-19; last entry 17:00, closed Wednesdays. Then walk the working diamond district by Centraal for the trade itself.

places.name: Het Steen
places.note: The city's oldest building, a 12th to 13th century fortress on the river; you cannot tour the inside, so treat it as the start of a riverside walk.

places.name: MoMu Fashion Museum
places.note: The Antwerp Six and the Royal Academy's fashion line, 13 euros, tickets until 17:00, closed Mondays. Nationalestraat outside is the independent designer strip.

places.name: Middelheim Museum
places.note: Free open-air sculpture park with Rodin, Moore and Ai Weiwei among the trees, 20 minutes on tram 32. Closed Mondays; closing runs from 17:00 in winter to 20:00 in midsummer.

places.name: De Koninck City Brewery
places.note: The self-guided hour round the Bolleke amber ale brewery, 19.90 euros with 2 tastings. Closed Mondays; the stemless round glass is the one to ask for in any Antwerp bar.

places.name: Frituur No. 1
places.note: The most reviewed fries stand in town at Hoogstraat 1; a cone with a frikandel or bicky burger on the side, eaten standing at the shelf. Cash is safest.

places.name: Grote Markt and Brabo Fountain
places.note: Guildhalls and the 1887 fountain of Brabo throwing the giant's hand that named the city. The terraces charge for the view: one coffee, then move on.

places.name: Vlaeykensgang
places.note: A 16th-century alley of old cobblers' workshops between Oude Koornmarkt and Hoogstraat. The entrance is easy to walk past; five quiet minutes a block from the cathedral crowd.

places.name: Kloosterstraat antiques strip
places.note: A few hundred metres of brocante and serious mid-century dealers. Most shops keep 10:00 to 18:00 and shut Sunday and Monday, but it goes shop by shop.

places.name: Antwerp Centraal Station
places.note: The 1905 hall with four platform levels stacked underneath. Free whenever you pass; look down from the main staircase toward the tracks.

places.name: Meir
places.note: The pedestrian high street from Centraal toward Groenplaats, 18th and 19th century facades and a former royal palace. Worst on Saturday afternoon.

places.name: Het Zuid brasserie dinner
places.note: Where Antwerp eats dinner, rather than on the Grote Markt terraces; order stoofvlees or vol-au-vent at a Flemish bistro. Book at weekends, the locals fill it.

places.name: Cogels-Osylei
places.note: A residential street of Belle Epoque and Art Nouveau townhouses, 1894 to 1914, each a different fantasy. 15 minutes by tram, few tourists, best in late afternoon light.

places.name: Sint-Jacobskerk
places.note: Rubens is buried here, in a chapel he designed behind an altarpiece with his own face among the saints. Skipped by the day-trippers; afternoon only in low season, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Zeevishandel De Eendracht
places.note: A fishmonger's counter on Hoogstraat, not a restaurant: order the kibbeling, fried to order for about 7.50 euros, and eat it standing there. Closed Sunday and Monday; the rest of the week hours vary, check, so go before mid-afternoon.

places.name: De 7 Schaken
places.note: A neighborhood restaurant tucked off the Grote Markt that locals still claim as theirs; order the stoofvlees, 24 euros and better than anything on the square 30 meters away. The kitchen shuts mid-afternoon between lunch and dinner, so a 16:00 walk-up finds the door locked; closed Mondays.

places.name: Belfry of Ghent
places.note: The 91m belfry with the gilded dragon, mostly by lift; 13 euros, 6.50 under 26. You climb for the three towers in a row: Belfry, St Bavo's, St Nicholas'.

places.name: Saint Bavo's Cathedral and the Ghent Altarpiece
places.note: The restored Van Eyck Mystic Lamb of 1432 in its own visitor centre. Altarpiece entry closes at 16:30 and Sunday opens at 13:00; book a timed ticket in summer.

places.name: Gravensteen
places.note: A moated 1180s castle whose battlements you can walk; 15 euros with an audio guide, take the comic track. Last entry 16:40, closed 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January.

places.name: Graslei and Korenlei
places.note: The two grain quays facing each other across the Leie, guildhouse facades end to end. Come at sunset, when the floodlights come on and the day-trip coaches have gone.

places.name: Design Museum Gent
places.note: An 18th-century mansion plus a modern wing, from Rococo rooms to Panton and Belgian design; under-18s free. Closing day and hours vary, check.

places.name: STAM Ghent City Museum
places.note: The city's history in the old Bijloke abbey with a glass extension; the big city model is the highlight. 15 minutes' walk south, closed Mondays, hours vary, check.

places.name: Dulle Griet
places.note: Order the Max, a litre of strong beer on a wooden stand; they keep one of your shoes in a basket at the ceiling until the glass comes back. Loud and packed on weekend nights.

places.name: Vrijdagmarkt
places.note: The medieval Friday Market square of gatherings and executions; food and general market on Fridays and Saturdays, cafes and guild houses the rest of the week.

places.name: Werregarenstraat (Graffiti Street)
places.note: An alley where spraying is legal and protected by the city, so it is different every visit. Five minutes between the Belfry and Vrijdagmarkt.

places.name: Tierenteyn-Verlent
places.note: Mustard made here since 1790, scooped from wooden barrels into the jar; a small one is 5 to 6 euros. A real family shop by the Vleeshuis, closed Sundays.

places.name: Patershol dinner
places.note: The old tanners' quarter, now the densest run of good restaurants in town; order Gentse waterzooi, chicken or fish in cream and egg yolk. Book at weekends.

places.name: Vier Tafels
places.note: The Patershol room locals name for waterzooi; small, so book. Its weekly closing day is not confirmed, so check before you pin a night on it.

places.name: Frites and cuberdons
places.note: A cone of fries from a frituur by the Belfry and a bag of cuberdons, the purple raspberry noses sold from carts. Cart hours vary; midday to evening is safest.

places.name: Waterzooi lunch at Groentenmarkt
places.note: Lunch terraces facing the medieval meat hall, calmer than Sint-Baafsplein. Waterzooi or stoofvlees with fries is the order at any of them.

places.name: 't Dreupelkot
places.note: A tiny jenever bar by the Graslei with over 200 genevers, mostly standing room; one strong glass after the sunset walk. Evenings are the safe bet; hours vary, check.

places.name: Boekentoren
places.note: Henry van de Velde's 1942 university library tower, restored. Free to look at from outside; the rooftop opens only on occasional open days, so check the university calendar.

places.name: Citadelpark
places.note: The biggest park in town on a 19th-century citadel site, with SMAK and the Fine Arts museum on its edges. Free, and joggers and families instead of coaches.

places.name: Sint-Niklaaskerk
places.note: The third of Ghent's three towers, 13th-century Scheldt Gothic in blue-grey Tournai stone. Free and right on the Korenmarkt to Belfry route, yet the least visited.

places.name: Belfry of Bruges
places.note: 366 steps, no lift, one-way traffic on the spiral; 15 euros. Summer hours to 2 November; in winter it runs 10:00 to 18:00 except Saturday. Climb before 09:30 or after 17:00 to miss the queue.

places.name: Basilica of the Holy Blood
places.note: A Romanesque lower chapel under a Gothic upper one holding a 12th-century blood relic. Free; the treasury is 5 euros, and the upper-chapel queue moves fast. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Groeninge Museum
places.note: Van Eyck, Memling and Gerard David in small dense rooms; 15 euros, 13 under 26. Closed Wednesdays, and never as crowded as its name even at midday.

places.name: De Halve Maan Brewery
places.note: Brugse Zot since 1856, with a 3.2km pipeline pumping beer under the old town. The 45-minute tour is 16 euros with one beer and 220 steps to the roof; the 90-minute XL is weekends only, 26.

places.name: Choco-Story
places.note: Cacao from the Maya to the praline, with a live demo and tasting; 13 euros, last entry 16:00. The 19 euro chocolate walk ticket adds two shop tastings.

places.name: Canal boat tour
places.note: 30 minutes round the canal ring for facades you cannot see from the street; 15 euros. March to October only, one jetty in winter; the queue builds after 11:00, try the Wollestraat dock.

places.name: Rozenhoedkaai
places.note: The canal corner with the belfry behind it that is on every postcard. From mid-morning it is selfie sticks; come at 07:00 to 08:00 or after dinner.

places.name: Begijnhof
places.note: The UNESCO 13th-century beguinage, white houses round a quiet lawn, now home to Benedictine nuns. Free; the house museum is extra. Quiet even in summer.

places.name: Minnewater
places.note: The medieval harbour basin turned swan lake, just south of the Begijnhof. Free and open all hours; do the two as one quiet loop.

places.name: Church of Our Lady
places.note: Michelangelo's Madonna and Child of about 1504, the only one to leave Italy in his lifetime, plus the tombs of Charles the Bold and Mary of Burgundy; the nave is free, the museum about 8 euros. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Frituur De Gentpoorte
places.note: Reviewers' pick for the best fries in town, away from the square's tourist prices; double fried in beef fat. No seats, bring cash.

places.name: De Garre
places.note: Down one of the narrowest alleys between Markt and Burg; the 11% Tripel van De Garre comes with a cheese cube, and it is one glass at a time. Hours vary, check.

places.name: 't Zwart Huis
places.note: Dinner in a 15th-century merchant house just off Markt. Menu and closing day unconfirmed; hours vary, check before you book.

places.name: Vismarkt
places.note: North Sea fish under 19th-century colonnades, mornings only, with craft stalls at weekends. Thin on Sundays and Mondays.

places.name: Lace shops, Balstraat
places.note: By the Lace Center, where the handwork is shown. Real handmade lace runs to hundreds of euros; the cheap stuff on Markt is machine-made, so buy where they can show you the maker.

places.name: Kruisvest windmills walk
places.note: A grass path along the old ramparts past all four surviving mills, Sint-Janshuismolen still working. Free and mostly locals; hire a bike near the station and go early or at dusk.

places.name: Evening drink on Wijngaardplein
places.note: A few small cafes by the Begijnhof gate and the carriage stand, calmer than Markt, with a canal view. Pick any; hours vary, check.

places.name: St Salvator's Cathedral
places.note: The town's oldest parish church, a cathedral since 1834, with tapestries and paintings behind the choir. Quieter than Our Lady; afternoons may be closed, hours vary, check.

places.name: In den Wittenkop
places.note: A small brasserie off Sint-Jakobsstraat that has run the same short, homemade menu for decades; order the eel in green sauce or the chicken supreme. A handful of tables and no guarantee of a walk-in seat on a Friday, and hours vary, check before you go.

places.name: Den Amand
places.note: A quiet bistro on Sint-Amandsstraat, a block from the Markt but priced and paced like it is not; order the pork cheek stew in Burgundy ale over the fish of the day. A handful of tables, so book, and it is shut Sundays and Wednesdays; the rest of the week hours vary, check.
